title: Guide - A Thankful Heart - Counting small mercies

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to A Thankful Heart. <short pause> This practice is called Counting Small Mercies. <short pause> You don't need a wonderful day for this. <short pause> An ordinary one will do... <short pause> even one that has only just begun.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let yourself settle where you are. <short pause> Loosen your shoulders, and take an easy breath. <short pause> There is nothing to produce in these few minutes, and no list you have to finish. <short pause> We are only going to look slowly at what is already here.

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: Small mercies are easy to miss, because they behave so well. <short pause> The tap runs, and we don't think about water. <short pause> The light comes on. <short pause> A knee that hurt last month carries us up the stairs. <short pause> A trouble gets our attention by knocking. <short pause> A mercy often lets itself in quietly... and puts the kettle on.

Perhaps that is why David, in Psalm one hundred three, has to talk to his own soul. <short pause> He doesn't tell it to go and find new blessings. <short pause> He tells it to remember the ones it has. <short pause> These are his words, from verse two.
Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Forget not. <short pause> It is such a gentle instruction. <short pause> It assumes the gifts have been given. <short pause> And it knows how quickly a busy heart forgets them. <short pause> So let's do a little remembering, together with God.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Begin as close as your own body. <short pause> One breath, arriving without being asked. <short pause> Thank You. <short pause> Your eyes, or your ears, or the hands that have done so much for you. <short pause> Choose one. <short pause> Thank You. <short pause> Whatever is holding your weight right now. <short pause> Thank You.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now widen the circle to the room. <short pause> Something that keeps you warm, or dry, or safe. <short pause> Thank You. <short pause> Something you use each day and almost never notice... a spoon, a key, a pair of worn shoes. <short pause> Thank You. <short pause> Something in view that is lovely for no useful reason at all. <short pause> Thank You.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: And now, a person. <short pause> Someone who made your life a little lighter, perhaps without knowing it. <short pause> They held a door. They answered. They stayed. <short pause> Let their face come to mind for a moment... <short pause> and instead of hurrying on, say their name to God. <short pause> Thank You, Lord, for them.

Is there a mercy that would have been an answered prayer, some years ago? <short pause> Something you once longed for, that has since become ordinary? <short pause> A home, a friend, a skill, a little more peace than you used to have. <short pause> See if you can meet it again, as if it had only just arrived.

You may have found only one thing. <short pause> One is not too few. <short pause> Thankfulness isn't measured by the length of the list. <short pause> It begins whenever a gift leads your eyes back to the Giver... <short pause> and one spoon, truly noticed, can do that.

Let's pray. <short pause> Generous God, <short pause> forgive me for walking past so much kindness. <short pause> Thank You for the mercies I counted, and the many more I will never see. <short pause> Slow my eyes. <short pause> Soften my heart. <short pause> And help my soul to forget not all that You have done. <short pause> Amen.

As you go back to your day, let one ordinary thing interrupt you. <short pause> Water on your hands. A light in a window. <short pause> When it does, you only need two words... <short pause> thank You. <short pause> Go gently, and keep noticing.
